cohort: All births in the United States' Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project-Nationwide Inpatient Sample from 2003 to 2011
finding: Pregnant women with Addison's disease had a significantly increased risk of various adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including preterm delivery, cesarean section, infections, thromboembolism, and maternal mortality.
mod_finding: Women with AD were more likely to deliver preterm (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.16-1.95) and deliver by cesarean section (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.08-1.61).
